short: The first major airborne invasion in military history, resulting in a German capture of the strategic Mediterranean island.
full:
On 20 May 1941, German paratroopers and glider-borne infantry launched a massive airborne assault on the Greek island of Crete. They were met by fierce resistance from British, Commonwealth, and Greek forces, as well as armed civilians. After suffering staggering casualties on the first day, German forces managed to secure the Maleme airfield, allowing them to fly in reinforcements and heavy equipment.

The capture of the airfield turned the tide of the battle, forcing the Allies into a fighting retreat across the island and another seaborne evacuation. Although a tactical success, the German airborne forces suffered such high losses that Adolf Hitler forbade any future large-scale airborne operations. The loss of Crete cemented Axis dominance in the eastern Mediterranean until late in the war.
